_note: Retreat planning checklist. Each task maps to a Notion card: phase, workstream, owner, essential and a link to its Playbook topic.
title: Retreat planning checklist
lead: Every task to do or consider for a training retreat, in order, from the first conversation to the ninety-day check. Each one links to the topic that explains it.

phases.name: Arrive and set up
phases.when: The day before, and the first morning

tasks.title: Find out what the retreat is really for
tasks.detail: Interview the sponsor and two or three attendees. Write the purpose in one sentence.

tasks.title: Decide whether going away is the right answer
tasks.detail: Run the decision test. A day in the office or a series of sessions may do the job better.

tasks.title: Agree what success looks like
tasks.detail: Name two or three changes you would see at work, and how you will know.

tasks.title: Name the sponsor and who decides
tasks.detail: One person signs off the purpose, the budget and the changes.

tasks.title: Agree who attends, and how many
tasks.detail: Group size shapes the venue, the staffing and the format.

tasks.title: Set the budget envelope
tasks.detail: Total, including travel and people's time, before you look at venues.

tasks.title: Choose the format and length
tasks.detail: Residential or day-based, how many nights, and what sits before and after.

tasks.title: Pick the season and rough dates
tasks.detail: Check daylight, weather, school holidays, financial year end and religious festivals.

tasks.title: Plan to cut travel and carbon
tasks.detail: Choose a location most people can reach by train, and count the travel in the decision.

tasks.title: Check whether your contract allows this work
tasks.detail: If you are employed, read your contract for outside work, competition and intellectual property.

tasks.title: Write the proposal
tasks.detail: The client's situation in their words, what you will do, what they must do, price and what is excluded.

tasks.title: Cost every line and set the price
tasks.detail: Venue, food, travel, staff, materials, contingency and your margin.

tasks.title: Shortlist venues against the brief
tasks.detail: Rooms for plenary and small groups, outdoor space, step-free access, food, quiet, travel links.

tasks.title: Visit the venue before you book
tasks.detail: Walk every space you will use, at the time of day you will use it.

tasks.title: Agree who signs the venue contract
tasks.detail: Decide who carries the risk of cancellation, minimum numbers and damage.

tasks.title: Read the cancellation and attrition terms
tasks.detail: Know the dates when deposits become non-refundable and the minimum numbers you must pay for.

tasks.title: Sign your terms with the client
tasks.detail: Scope, fees, payment dates, cancellation, intellectual property and data.

tasks.title: Check your insurance covers it
tasks.detail: Public liability, professional indemnity, and cover for outdoor activities if you run them.

tasks.title: Book the facilitators and staff
tasks.detail: Lead, second facilitator, and anyone for wellbeing, movement or outdoor sessions.

tasks.title: Put the dates in everyone's diary
tasks.detail: Include travel time and the follow-up session.

tasks.title: Plan what personal data you need
tasks.detail: Collect only what you will use, say why, and decide when you will delete it.

tasks.title: Set up the project tracker
tasks.detail: One shared place for tasks, owners, dates and risks.

tasks.title: Design the before, during and after
tasks.detail: Pre-work and a manager conversation before; follow-up sessions after.

tasks.title: Build the timetable
tasks.detail: Hardest work when energy is highest, real breaks, nothing intense after dinner.

tasks.title: Design for absorption, not intensity
tasks.detail: Fewer, deeper sessions with time to practise and talk.

tasks.title: Plan how trust builds before openness
tasks.detail: Start with low-risk activities. Ask for personal stories later, never first.

tasks.title: Choose the methods for each session
tasks.detail: Match each session to its objective. Use the recipes for a starting point.

tasks.title: Agree how decisions will be made
tasks.detail: For a working offsite: who decides, and what happens to ideas that are not chosen.

tasks.title: Plan the outdoor sessions, with a wet-weather version
tasks.detail: Use the outdoors for a reason, and have an indoor plan for every outdoor slot.

tasks.title: Build in time alone to reflect
tasks.detail: Short solo time with a prompt, especially after intense sessions.

tasks.title: Offer movement people can choose
tasks.detail: Optional, varied in intensity, and with a way to take part for everyone.

tasks.title: Add play that serves the point
tasks.detail: Games and play with a clear link to the learning.

tasks.title: Set the rules for evenings, alcohol and free time
tasks.detail: Evenings optional, a good alcohol-free offer, and a clear end time for organised events.

tasks.title: Plan the evenings
tasks.detail: Food, a fire, a walk or a conversation people can join or skip.

tasks.title: Set the rules for phones and contact with work
tasks.detail: Agree with the sponsor when people can check in, and say so in advance.

tasks.title: Include people who cannot stay overnight
tasks.detail: Caring responsibilities, health or faith: design a version that works for them.

tasks.title: Give managers a job before, during and after
tasks.detail: A conversation before, time released during, and questions to ask after.

tasks.title: Plan the close and the return to work
tasks.detail: A first-use plan for each person and a date for the follow-up.

tasks.title: List the materials and kit
tasks.detail: Flipcharts, cards, pens, printed handouts, outdoor kit, speakers.

tasks.title: Run a pre-mortem on the design
tasks.detail: Imagine it went badly. List why, and change the design for the top three.

tasks.title: Write the duty-of-care plan
tasks.detail: What people are told, consent, limits of your role, signs someone needs support, who to call.

tasks.title: Do the risk assessment
tasks.detail: Every activity, the venue, travel and the outdoors. Review it when anything changes.

tasks.title: Write the incident plan
tasks.detail: Who is in charge, the contact sheet, what to do and how to record it.

tasks.title: Arrange first aid cover
tasks.detail: A trained first aider on site, and the nearest hospital and pharmacy noted.

tasks.title: Brief and check everyone you bring in
tasks.detail: Facilitators and suppliers get the purpose, the plan, the rules and the safety plan.

tasks.title: Collect access, dietary and other needs
tasks.detail: Ask once, privately, and only for what you will act on.

tasks.title: Plan the rooms
tasks.detail: Single rooms by default, and accessible rooms where needed.

tasks.title: Plan travel and transfers
tasks.detail: Train times, pick-ups, parking, and a plan for late arrivals.

tasks.title: Describe the retreat honestly
tasks.detail: Promise the conditions, never the transformation.

tasks.title: Send the joining instructions
tasks.detail: Purpose, timetable outline, what to bring, travel, accessibility, phones, evenings and who to contact.

tasks.title: Confirm final numbers with the venue
tasks.detail: Check the deadline in the contract.

tasks.title: Send the venue the full brief
tasks.detail: Room layouts, timings, meals, dietary list, access needs, kit and quiet hours.

tasks.title: Write the run sheet
tasks.detail: Minute by minute for each day, with who does what.

tasks.title: Brief the staff team
tasks.detail: Walk through the run sheet, roles, the duty-of-care plan and what to do if.

tasks.title: Prepare and print materials
tasks.detail: Flipcharts drawn in advance, cards cut, handouts printed.

tasks.title: Send the pre-work
tasks.detail: Short, useful and something you will use on day one.

tasks.title: Prompt managers to have the before conversation
tasks.detail: Send them two questions to ask.

tasks.title: Check in with the sponsor
tasks.detail: Any changes in the business, the group or the purpose since you designed it.

tasks.title: Check the weather and adjust
tasks.detail: Swap to the indoor versions where needed and tell people what to bring.

tasks.title: Print the contact and emergency sheet
tasks.detail: Venue lead, staff, client contact, first aider, local services.

tasks.title: Arrive early and walk the venue
tasks.detail: Every room, the outdoor spaces, toilets, exits and the route people will take.

tasks.title: Meet the venue lead
tasks.detail: Run through timings, meals, the dietary list and who to call.

tasks.title: Set up the rooms
tasks.detail: Furniture, walls, materials and a space for quiet.

tasks.title: Test the technology
tasks.detail: Screen, sound, wifi and anything online, with a back-up with no technology.

tasks.title: Put the incident sheet and log in place
tasks.detail: Everyone on the team knows where they are.

tasks.title: Mark the start
tasks.detail: Open with the purpose, the rules and what people will leave with.

tasks.title: Hold a staff check-in every day
tasks.detail: Morning and evening: energy, concerns, changes to the plan.

tasks.title: Watch energy and adjust the timetable
tasks.detail: Cut or move sessions rather than run over.

tasks.title: Record decisions, owners and dates on the wall
tasks.detail: For working offsites, photograph them at the end of each day.

tasks.title: Keep the incident log
tasks.detail: Write down anything that happens and what you did.

tasks.title: Keep evenings optional
tasks.detail: Check that people who leave early are not left out of anything that matters.

tasks.title: Close with a first-use plan
tasks.detail: Each person writes what they will do in the first week back.

tasks.title: Collect feedback before people leave
tasks.detail: Short, and about what they will use, not only how they felt.

tasks.title: Mark the end
tasks.detail: A clear close before travel, not a fade-out.

tasks.title: Send the write-up
tasks.detail: Within 48 hours: decisions, owners, dates and what happens next.

tasks.title: Brief managers on what to ask
tasks.detail: Two questions for the first week back.

tasks.title: Thank everyone
tasks.detail: Attendees, staff, venue and suppliers.

tasks.title: Debrief with the staff team
tasks.detail: What worked, what to change, and any incidents to follow up.

tasks.title: Read the feedback and send a short summary
tasks.detail: To the sponsor, with what you will change.

tasks.title: Reconcile the costs
tasks.detail: Check the venue invoice against the contract, pay suppliers, send your invoice.

tasks.title: Share photos only with consent
tasks.detail: Ask before sharing, and remove anyone who says no.

tasks.title: Run the follow-up session
tasks.detail: Recall, what has been tried, what got in the way.

tasks.title: Check what people are doing differently
tasks.detail: Against the success measures you agreed at the start.

tasks.title: Review the decisions from the offsite
tasks.detail: Which are done, which are stuck, and who will unstick them.

tasks.title: Report results to the sponsor
tasks.detail: Short, in their terms, with what you would do next time.

tasks.title: Gather a case study, with consent
tasks.detail: One or two stories of real change you can share.

tasks.title: Close out and hand over
tasks.detail: Final report, files, what the client keeps and who owns what next.

tasks.title: Delete the personal data you no longer need
tasks.detail: On the date you set at the start.

tasks.title: Update this checklist
tasks.detail: Add what you learned, so the next retreat starts better.
